name: Jimmy "Cash" Cerone
caption: A Chicago wrestler eliminated in the opening round of the promotion's own founding tournament by Arthur Essex's Crossed Swords submission.

tenures.source: Loses to Arthur Essex in a first-round tournament match on Monday Night Elite (12 October 1998).

name: "Dangerous" Damien Cooper
caption: A St. Louis wrestler eliminated in the opening round of the promotion's own founding tournament by Westside Walavan.

tenures.source: Loses to Westside Walavan in a first-round tournament match on Monday Night Elite (12 October 1998).

name: Brian "Farmdawg" Farmer
caption: A Milwaukee-based wrestler eliminated from the founding tournament by Shawn Crimson, later on the losing end of a Television Championship tournament match stopped by outside interference.

tenures.source: Loses to Shawn Crimson in a first-round tournament match on Monday Night Elite (12 October 1998); loses a Television Championship tournament match to Westside Walavan by disqualification after Arthur Essex runs in, on Monday Night Elite (16 November 1998).

name: "Simply Perfect" James Miller
caption: A second-generation Georgia wrestler who used a chair shot and a handful of powder to become the promotion's first Americas Heavyweight Champion.

tenures.source: Loses to James Pillow in a first-round tournament match on Monday Night Elite (12 October 1998); loses a non-tournament match to Jack Vars on Monday Night Elite (19 October 1998); loses a non-tournament match to Westside Walavan on Monday Night Elite (26 October 1998); defeats James Pillow, then defeats an interfering Tony Paseno with a chair shot after blinding Pillow with powder, to become the first Americas Heavyweight Champion on Monday Night Elite (16 November 1998).

name: Matty Dee
caption: A former Global Wrestling Alliance World Heavyweight Champion, ejected from the promotion's own debut broadcast by its president before returning to lose a grudge match to Arthur Essex.

tenures.source: Ejected from the arena by IEWC President Dusty Love on Monday Night Elite (12 October 1998); returns to lose a non-tournament match to Arthur Essex, then is chair-shotted by Justin Miller after the bell, on Monday Night Elite (26 October 1998).

name: Mr. Submission
caption: A masked, heavily booed Television Championship tournament entrant, still carrying a rival promotion's Cruiserweight title belt, who submitted an ambushing Bobby Drake.

tenures.source: Defeats Bobby Drake, who ambushed him before the bell, in a tournament match on Monday Night Elite (16 November 1998).

name: Robyn Madden
caption: Arthur Essex's valet, an outspoken presence in his feud with IEWC President Dusty Love dating back to the two's shared time in the ICW.

tenures.source: Accompanies Arthur Essex and cuts a promo against Dusty Love on Monday Night Elite (12 October 1998); continues to accompany Essex through the promotion's autumn 1998 tournament run.

name: John Hamilton
caption: The promotion's face commentator, calling Monday Night Elite alongside Dan Gibbons for the length of the promotion's own founding tournament.

tenures.source: Calls play-by-play on every Monday Night Elite broadcast in the held record (12, 19, 26 October and 16 November 1998).

name: Dan Gibbons
caption: The promotion's color commentator, calling Monday Night Elite alongside John Hamilton for the length of the promotion's own founding tournament.

tenures.source: Calls color commentary on every Monday Night Elite broadcast in the held record (12, 19, 26 October and 16 November 1998).

name: Robert Bowen
caption: The promotion's ring announcer for the length of its own founding tournament.

tenures.source: Announces every match on every Monday Night Elite broadcast in the held record (12, 19, 26 October and 16 November 1998).

name: IEWC Owner
caption: The promotion's on-air owner, who announced the tournament final and its winner's prize -- the promotion's own first World Heavyweight Championship -- in the ring.

tenures.source: Appears in the ring on Monday Night Elite (26 October 1998) to announce that the tournament final between CandyMan and Shawn Crimson, the following week, will crown the promotion's own first-ever World Heavyweight Champion.

name: "Excellent" Arthur Essex
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1999: #145, tagged USW. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Came in at #145 in the RSPWF Top 200 for 1999.

tenures.source: Billed in-story as "The Dark Knight" Arthur Essex, feuding with IEWC President Dusty Love over a "short feud in the ICW" -- matching this record's own existing RSPWF Top 200 poll corroboration of an ICW background -- across Monday Night Elite (12, 19, 26 October and 16 November 1998); the promotion's own video package narrates an earlier in-story moniker change from "Dark Horse" to "Dark Knight," consistent with this record's own differing "Excellent" qualifier reflecting a still earlier persona of the same name.

name: "The Natural" Justin Miller
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1998: #20, tagged OWF, HHWO. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Ranked #20 in the RSPWF Top 200 for 1998.

tenures.source: Billed in-story as "The Natural" Justin Miller -- matching this record's own existing nickname exactly -- runs in to attack both Arthur Essex and Matty Dee after Essex's non-tournament win, aligning with IEWC President Dusty Love, on Monday Night Elite (26 October 1998).

name: Westside Walavan
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1998: #92, tagged ICW, WWO, ASW, FWF; 1999: #112, tagged ICW. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Placed in two editions of the RSPWF Top 200 — #92 in 1998, #112 in 1999 — best at #92.

identity.note: The registry's own decorated-aka guard reads this name as a normalized substring match against the-westside. Recorded distinct, not merged: the only record this entity has is a placing in the RSPWF Top 200, which gives a ring name and a federation tag and nothing else — no dates, no roster, no URL, so three of the collision doctrine's own four signals are simply absent and the no-merge default holds. Every held-promotion roster the ranked names were checked against came back with zero overlap. Reopenable the moment either side gains a record the other can be checked against.

tenures.source: Billed in-story as a "former ICW Television Champion" -- matching this record's own existing RSPWF Top 200 poll corroboration of an ICW background -- Westside Walavan wins his tournament opener, then loses in the quarterfinals to Arthur Essex, then wins a Television Championship tournament match over Brian Farmer by disqualification after Essex interferes, across Monday Night Elite (12, 19 October and 16 November 1998).
